extracted.intended_audience: research administrators, university leaders, funding agency program officers, interdisciplinary scientists and trainees
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on identifying barriers to interdisciplinary research and concrete recommendations for funding agencies and universities to enable interdisciplinary research and training across the brain, behavioral, and clinical sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and address attitudinal resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Most scientists recognize a need for interdisciplinary research, many are reluctant to abandon their disciplinary focus; interdisciplinary science is perceived by some as 'second-rate' or 'less challenging' and may threaten professional identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge perceptions (e.g., loss of identity, 'jack of all trades' fears) and actively counter them through education, incentives, and leadership examples. Examples: highlight successful interdisciplinary careers; document cases where disciplinary depth and interdisciplinary breadth jointly advanced knowledge. Anti-pattern: treating interdisciplinarity as fashionable without addressing underlying tenure/promotion incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcome disciplinary jargon and language barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists learn a discipline-specific language; the same terms may mean different things across fields and disciplines can rediscover one another's discoveries under different names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time in mutual education: require team members to learn others' terminology and to teach their own. Facilitate glossaries, cross-disciplinary seminars, and extended communication time. Beware of assuming comprehension when terms look similar across fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect other disciplines and mitigate intellectual turf issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Pride in one's discipline can lead to viewing other disciplines as less rigorous; heated disputes may arise when asserting correctness across backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote mutual appreciation of methods and limitations; include conflict-moderation practices and training; select leaders who can mediate and validate differing methodological perspectives. Anti-pattern: privileging one discipline's methods in decision-making without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build effective interdisciplinary teams with clear roles and processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Teamwork requires trust in another's skills; interdisciplinary team members sometimes have difficulty evaluating each other's performance because evaluation criteria are unfamiliar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify roles, expectations, authority, data/resource sharing, and decision processes early. Develop mutually acceptable dissemination and authorship policies to facilitate members' professional goals. Provide interpersonal and communication skills training. Scoring note: strong teams show documented role clarity, agreed authorship rules, and regular structured communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership suited to interdisciplinary teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders need vision, creativity, perseverance, credibility as research scientists, skill in modulating personalities, and the ability to blend individual strengths into a team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer mature scientists with established research careers and interdisciplinary experience to direct teams; provide leadership development focused on group dynamics. Measure success by leaders' ability to coordinate diverse expertise and to educate colleagues and administrators about interdisciplinary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate interactions through physical and virtual proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Chance interactions (coffee machine, corridor, seminars) and common facilities promote interdisciplinary collaborations; architectural design and virtual proximity (Internet, videoconferencing) can increase intellectual proximity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund and design shared facilities, common spaces, and virtual collaboration tools. Examples: shared imaging facilities, colocated labs, interdisciplinary building projects. Anti-pattern: isolated laboratory buildings that inhibit informal exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt academic structures to support interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities are partitioned along academic lines (departments) that affect teaching, recruitment, promotion, and resource allocation; departmental structures and funding processes can inhibit interdisciplinary approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement cross-departmental programs/centers, joint positions, and institutional policies that recognize and reward interdisciplinary contributions. Ensure administrative commitment (space, funds, positions) for interdisciplinary efforts. Assessment: presence of formal interdisciplinary units, joint hires, and institutional resource commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate fair credit and overhead for interdisciplinary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions vary in how they distribute credit for successful grants; some credit only the PI, penalizing coinvestigators in other departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt policies to fairly allocate research overhead and to credit home departments of all investigators; explicitly account for interdisciplinary contributions in resource distribution. Scoring: transparent overhead allocation rules and documented credit practices for collaborative grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise promotion and tenure policies to not impede interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotion and tenure policies, which emphasize publications and grants within disciplinary structures, can discourage junior faculty from interdisciplinary work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and revise appointment, promotion, and tenure criteria to value interdisciplinary research and teaching. Examples: include documented interdisciplinary outputs, defined contributions on multi-author works, and flexibility in review timelines. Anti-pattern: evaluating interdisciplinary candidates solely by single-discipline norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide publication outlets and authorship transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals and professional organizations shape disciplinary identity and constrain topics and methods; collaborative groups can limit first-authorship frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage journals and societies to recognize interdisciplinary work; adopt editorial policies that define and acknowledge individual contributions to multi-author papers. Scoring: use of author-contribution statements and presence of interdisciplinary journals/societies for dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design funding mechanisms to require institutional commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement of institutional commitment (supportive promotion policies, appropriate overhead, shared facilities) as a condition for funding bolsters university support for interdisciplinary efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding agencies should ask for statements of institutional commitment (space, infrastructure, priority mechanisms) in grant applications (examples: NSF IGERT, NCI SPORE). Monitor whether such requirements change institutional behaviors like tenure policy adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support peer review structures that fairly evaluate interdisciplinary proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review can disadvantage interdisciplinary proposals when discipline-specific study sections lack appropriate breadth or reviewers lack interdisciplinary experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use review groups that include scientists from multiple disciplines who are actively engaged in interdisciplinary research; design integrated review groups (IRGs) to encompass necessary expertise; monitor peer review reforms for impact on interdisciplinary funding outcomes. Example: NIH's creation of IRGs and Panel on Scientific Boundaries for Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate interagency and public–private partnerships for broad support
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinary research funds come from many agencies with different emphases; partnerships among agencies or between public and private sectors provide a broad base of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage and continue collaborations among institutes/agencies and with industry to support interdisciplinary projects. Assessment: existence of cross-agency RFAs and joint funding initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate training as integral to interdisciplinary research funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding announcements should indicate that training is an integral component of the interdisciplinary research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require or encourage training plans within interdisciplinary grant proposals to ensure workforce development. Scoring: presence and quality of training components in funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate career barriers: training duration, debt, and job market concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of training for multiple fields, high educational debt, and concerns about market demand deter trainees from interdisciplinary careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide financial incentives (loan repayment programs), career-development support, and transparent information about job markets. Examples: expand LRPs beyond NIH; provide career-placement services highlighting industry demand. Anti-pattern: expecting trainees to bear extended training time without compensation or clear career pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide midcareer retraining and continuing education opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Midcareer scientists face difficulty retooling; funding mechanisms are needed to allow updating or retraining in other fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create targeted funding and fellowship opportunities for midcareer scientists to acquire new disciplinary skills sufficient to be productive team members. Evaluation: availability and uptake of retraining grants or programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address special challenges of clinician–scientists in interdisciplinary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinician–scientists face long clinical training, debt, low academic salaries, and longer lead times for interdisciplinary projects to produce publishable results, which complicates promotion and participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tailored support: loan repayment programs, protected research time, modified promotion timelines, and targeted funding. Anti-pattern: expecting early-career clinicians to undertake long interdisciplinary projects without adjustments to promotion clocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use infrastructure and technology to help researchers stay current across fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Growth in publications makes keeping current in multiple fields daunting; online journals, citation services, and electronic forums can help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund access to online journals, citation alert services (e.g., Cite Trak), and electronic discussion forums/bulletin boards to ease cross-field literature surveillance. Scoring: institutional subscriptions and recommended tools provided to interdisciplinary teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote interdisciplinary centers, institutes, and programs where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinary institutes and centers formally recognize interdisciplinary endeavors and can cross departmental barriers, but they require sustained institutional commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage development, maintenance, and evolution of interdisciplinary centers for problems suited to cross-disciplinary approaches; ensure administrative support to prevent drift back to single-discipline perspectives. Assessment: existence, resourcing, and longevity of interdisciplinary centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution: encourage interdisciplinarity only to solve appropriate problems
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee cautions that interdisciplinary research should not be encouraged for its own sake but, rather, to solve appropriate research problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate projects on whether interdisciplinary approaches are necessary and likely to add value for the research question. Anti-pattern: promoting interdisciplinarity as an end rather than as a means to address problems that require multiple perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require policies for authorship and contributor acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: New editorial policies on authorship are arising to define contributions of each author and to protect against fraud; acknowledging individual contributions might provide credit beyond senior authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt author contribution statements and transparent criteria for authorship within teams and journals; institutions and funders should value these documented contributions in evaluation processes.
